-73.99310,40.73700.name: Kindbody-New York
-73.99310,40.73700.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Aimee Seungdamrong, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

0.12828,52.19529.name: London Women's Clinic, Cambridge
0.12828,52.19529.state: Woodlands Surgery, 48-49 Bateman Street, Cambridge, Cambridgeshire, CB2 1LR
0.12828,52.19529.company: Satellite clinic to London Women's Clinic
0.12828,52.19529.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to London Women's Clinic. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-123.96564,49.15789.name: Vancouver Island University
-123.96564,49.15789.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, April 2024
-123.96564,49.15789.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, April 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-58.67382,-34.60415.name: Institute of Virology, National Institute of Agricultural Technology (INTA)
-58.67382,-34.60415.state: 98WG+8F William C. Morris, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina
-58.67382,-34.60415.company: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries
-58.67382,-34.60415.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on animal health. Operational or announced: 2009. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

77.68000,12.90800.name: Syngene International
77.68000,12.90800.desc: An Indian contract research and manufacturing company working for global pharmaceutical clients, part of the Biocon group. The scale of Indian contract research means a large fraction of the world’s preclinical data is generated here, and the regulator reading it is usually somewhere else entirely.

77.68000,12.90800.name: Biocon — biosimilar insulin
77.68000,12.90800.desc: Manufactures insulin in engineered organisms at prices far below the American market, supplying much of the developing world from India. Insulin was the first engineered consumer product, approved in 1982, and its patent expired decades ago — yet US list prices rose for years through incremental reformulation. The technology being old and cheap to make is not what determines what a patient pays.

16.37380,48.20820.name: AGES — Austrian Agency for Health and Food Safety
16.37380,48.20820.desc: Austria’s food and health agency, in a country that has been among the most consistently opposed to engineered crops in Europe and whose provinces have declared themselves GMO-free. Austria has used EU safeguard clauses to block specific approvals more often than any other member state.

16.37380,48.20820.name: Global 2000 / Friends of the Earth Austria
16.37380,48.20820.desc: The Austrian environmental organisation behind the country's long opposition to engineered crops, and the campaigning that made Austria the first EU member to invoke a national safeguard clause against an approved variety. Austria's stance later became the template for the opt-out mechanism written into EU law in 2015.

12.48700,41.88300.name: International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources (Plant Treaty)
12.48700,41.88300.state: Rome — FAO, Viale delle Terme di Caracalla
12.48700,41.88300.desc: The treaty governing access to the crop diversity everyone breeds from, and the multilateral system through which a breeder can take material from a genebank in one country and use it in another. It also carries the clause recognising farmers’ rights to save and exchange seed — which sits directly against what UPOV 91 requires, and countries have signed both. The contradiction is not an oversight; it is what happens when the same governments negotiate in two rooms.
